45	CASE OD2-DEV2-INTERACT: Larkfield DC: robot collision stops tripled in September

A robot logs a 'collision stop' (protective stop) whenever an obstacle enters its protective field. The analysis date is 20 October 2026.

49	Presenting request: The regional operations director writes: 'Larkfield's robot collision stops have roughly tripled since early September, in the middle of peak season. The GM wants a disciplinary policy for agency temps, and Halvane suggests shortening the robots' protective fields. Tell me what is actually driving the stops and what the site should do now.'

51	INITIAL EVIDENCE

A stop is logged whenever an obstacle enters a robot's protective field; the robot halts until the field clears, typically for 20–90 seconds. Physical contacts with people or equipment: 1 in weeks 30–35, 1 in weeks 37–41. Robot operating hours were roughly constant across the period.
53	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dana Okafor, General Manager, to site leadership, 5 October (leadership-account): Subject: Robot stops. 'The timing tells the story. Engineering keeps telling me it's the software, but Halvane says their update runs fine at other sites, so let's stop chasing that.'
54	E3 [stage S1] Change record CHG-2026-0412 (change-record): Fleet firmware upgrade, HR-7 6.3 to 6.4. Implemented 2–4 September 2026 on 50 of 58 robots. Vendor release summary: 'Revised near-field return filtering for improved detection of low-profile obstacles; navigation and charging fixes; security patches.' Halvane lifecycle notice: security support for 6.3 ends 31 October 2026. The eight exception units are covered by a time-limited waiver.
55	E4 [stage S1] Email from Halvane Robotics Customer Support (Tier 2), 25 September (vendor-account): 'We've reviewed your ticket. Firmware 6.4 has been live at three other customer sites since July with no change in protective-stop rates, so we don't see the firmware as the cause. Increases like this are usually environmental: people, layout, clutter. If the stops are hurting throughput, a common remedy is to shorten the protective field by 20%, and we can push that profile to your fleet remotely. Our next release, 6.4.2, is planned for early December and includes further filtering refinements.'

Somebody asked me about the new shiny pallet wrap; procurement switched suppliers at the start of August. I don't buy it. We had that wrap for a month before the stops went up and nothing changed. If it was the wrap, August would have been bad too.'

Outbound pallet volume has been up 18% since week 35 as the seasonal peak ramped. input.brief: The stops are driven by an interaction between the new firmware (6.4) and the glossy stretch film introduced in August. The firmware now keeps weak short-range reflections, and the glossy film produces them at oblique angles, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles. Evidence: in the bench test, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17/20 passes. 6.3 on gloss, or 6.4 on the old matte film, stopped 0–1/20. In the field, 6.4 pallet robots in Zones A/B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The 6.3 robots working the same zones stayed flat, as did 6.4 tote robots in Zone C, which has no wrapped pallets. Temps were present everywhere, so they do not explain the pattern. A discipline policy would punish the wrong people and hide information. Shortening the protective fields would weaken a safety control without fixing the cause. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: switch back to the previous matte film, keep the firmware, and track weekly stops by zone and firmware group. Have Halvane test 6.4.2 against the gloss film before relying on it. Keep the firmware rollback as a fallback if the film switch doesn't bring stops down. The link between stops and missed cut-offs is not proven. Peak volume also contributed, since cut-off misses rose last year with flat stops.
